article.articleHeadline: Kamineni Hospitals Warn of Monsoon Viral Fever Surge in Hyderabad
article.articleSummary: Hyderabad's monsoon-season surge of viral fevers is being observed at Kamineni Hospitals (LB Nagar, King Koti). Outpatient visits for viral fevers, influenza-like illness (ILI), and acute febrile conditions have spiked; clinicians urge early lab testing for fevers persisting beyond 72 hours and discourage indiscriminate antibiotic use. Hyderabad recorded 266 dengue cases (127 lab-confirmed) Jan–mid July 2026, down from 570 (2025) and 821 (2024). National data show dengue >33,000 and H1N1 >9,000 year-to-date, with influenza up ~11% versus July 2025. India has 178 H1N1 fatalities this year; a second post-monsoon flu peak is anticipated. High-risk groups (children, elderly, pregnant women, and those with diabetes, heart disease, or immunosuppression) require close monitoring; warning signs include bleeding, breathlessness, vomiting, reduced urine, and confusion. Dengue may be critical during days 3–7 as fever subsides. Prevention emphasizes vector control and respiratory hygiene; Kamineni Hospitals offer 24/7 testing and advocate influenza vaccination.

triage.headline_ja: カミネニ病院、ハイデラバードでのモンスーン期ウイルス性発熱・インフルエンザ増加を警告
triage.triage_reason: モンスーン季節性のウイルス性発熱・デング・H1N1増加に関する病院からの健康アドバイザリーであり、地域的には既知のパターン内だが、全国的なH1N1死亡者数や前年比インフルエンザ増加など注視すべき数値が含まれる。
triage.notes: デング症例数は前年・前々年より減少傾向。H1N1は全国で178人死亡、インフルエンザは前年同月比11%増との記述あり。ハイデラバード地域の病院による季節性アドバイザリー記事であり、突発的な異常事態や国際的拡大の兆候は明記されていない。

article.articleHeadline: Falta de centros de atención y rastreo de contactos complican la respuesta al ébola en RDC
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Lack of treatment centers and contact tracing complicates the Ebola response in the DRC.
article.articleSummary: Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) continues to spread from Ituri (epicenter) to Bas-Uélé, Tshopo, Haut-Uélé, North Kivu and South Kivu, with 5,713 confirmed cases and 2,744 deaths as of Aug 25, 2026; 1,269 recoveries and 770 still in isolation or in Ebola Treatment Centers (CTEs). Contact tracing stands at 84.6% (target 85%), reflecting weak surveillance, and insufficient treatment capacity and CTEs in some zones, compounded by demotivated workers unpaid at control points. The outbreak, declared May 15 in Ituri, is the second-deadliest in the region’s history, below the 2018–2020 crisis yet far from the 2014–2016 West Africa epidemic. DR Congo has received 16,520 Ervebo vaccines for Zaire ebolavirus; early animal data suggest potential activity against Bundibugyo, while two Bundibugyo vaccines are in Phase 1. Uganda reported 20 cases (15 imported from DRC) and two deaths before declaring the outbreak over. Ebola transmission is via direct contact with bodily fluids, causing fever, vomiting, diarrhea and hemorrhages.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国におけるエボラ対応、治療センター不足と接触者追跡の遅れが複雑化
triage.triage_reason: DRCで確定5,713例・死者2,744人の大規模エボラ流行が継続し、接触追跡率が目標未達で医療体制の不足も報告されており、国際的拡大（ウガンダへの輸出例）も確認されているためフルRRAが必要。
triage.notes: ウガンダやアンゴラは発生地域に含まれるが、記事の主題はDRC国内の流行拡大であり、ウガンダは輸入例による小規模流行で既に終息宣言済み。両国とも対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations には含めない。

article.articleHeadline: Nejčastější nechtěný suvenýr z prázdnin? Žloutenka!
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The most common unwanted souvenir from vacation? Jaundice!
article.articleSummary: Hepatitis A is described as the most common unwanted vacation souvenir for children, according to Dr. Jana Pavličíková of the Olomouc Region’s newly opened first pediatric infectious disease ambulance. Summer is also associated with diarrheal illnesses tied to travel and diet, and Lyme borreliosis is frequently addressed. The most exotic disease encountered by Prostějov doctors was dengue fever. A 16-year-old boy returned from a family vacation in Vietnam and developed symptoms after returning home; he recovered at home, with serological testing confirming dengue infection. Vaccination is emphasized as the best defense against this widespread souvenir, Hepatitis A. In the Olomouc region, eight-year-old Gabinka Štecová was vaccinated yesterday at the first pediatric infectious ambulance in the region.

triage.headline_ja: 休暇からの最もよくある望まれないお土産は？黄疸（A型肝炎）！
triage.triage_reason: チェコの地域医療における旅行関連感染症（A型肝炎、デング熱、ライム病）の一般的な啓発記事であり、公衆衛生上の異常事態や国際的拡大の懸念は認められない。
triage.notes: ベトナムはデング熱に感染した患者が旅行した先として言及されているが、感染事象自体はチェコ在住の個人症例であり、ベトナム国内での発生事象ではないため対象国リストに含めない。

article.articleHeadline: Число заболевших Эболой в ДР Конго превысило 5,7 тысяч человек
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The number of Ebola cases in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has surpassed 5,700.
article.articleSummary: In the Democratic Republic of Congo, Ebola confirmed cases have risen to 5,713 with 2,744 deaths since the outbreak began. The INSP daily update reports 57 new cases, 11 deaths, and 24 recoveries in the last 24 hours. Ituri and North Kivu provinces are the hardest hit, though health workers note underreporting as many patients die outside facilities. There is no licensed vaccine or treatment for the Bundibugyo Ebola strain driving this outbreak. A vaccine called Ervebo, distributed by WHO to DRC, may offer some protection, but it is not licensed for this Bundibugyo lineage. Ongoing surveillance and public health measures continue to address transmission, with figures reflecting confirmed cases, deaths, and recoveries to date.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国のエボラ感染者数が5,700人を超えた
triage.triage_reason: DRCで進行中のエボラ（ブンディブジョ株）流行が5,713例・死者2,744人に達し、致死率が高く未承認ワクチン・治療薬の状況下で拡大が続いているため、フルリスク評価が必要と判断。
triage.notes: ブンディブジョ株には承認済みワクチン・治療薬がなく、施設外死亡による過小報告の懸念も指摘されている。IturiとNorth Kivu州で被害が大きい。

article.articleHeadline: Manipur's Churachandpur Battles Triple Disease Outbreak, Medical Teams On Alert
article.articleSummary: Churachandpur district, Manipur, is battling a triple outbreak of dengue, typhoid and scrub typhus, with children among the hardest hit, following recent rainfall that favors spread. Government sources say more than 100 children have tested positive for dengue, while the state health directorate reports over 105 dengue-positive cases; total probable cases may be higher. Hospitals, including government and private facilities in Churachandpur town, are crowded; at Churachandpur District Hospital the pediatric ward is full, leading officials to consider using orthopaedic and surgical wards for feverish children. Private hospitals report similar strain. In response, schools across the district are closed until August 31 to curb transmission, with extensions possible if conditions do not improve. Preventive guidance emphasizes cleaning surroundings, eliminating stagnant water, using mosquito nets, drinking safe water to prevent typhoid, and seeking prompt medical care for high fever. Ongoing monitoring by medical teams continues.

triage.headline_ja: マニプール州チュラチャンプル、デング熱・腸チフス・ツツガムシ病の三重流行に苦戦、医療チームが警戒態勢
triage.triage_reason: デング熱・腸チフス・ツツガムシ病の同時流行により小児を中心に100人超が感染、病院が満床となり学校閉鎖などの行政対応が取られており、WPRO基準の複数該当と社会的関心の高まりが確認される。
triage.notes: デング・腸チフス・ツツガムシ病はいずれも季節性（雨季）に流行しやすい既知の疾患であり、国際的拡大や渡航制限のリスクは低いと考えられるが、地域内での医療体制への負荷（小児科病床不足、学校閉鎖）が確認され、地域内でのフルアセスメントに値する。

article.articleHeadline: Cegah Rabies, Puluhan Anjing Semi Liar di Mataram Jadi Sasaran Vaksinasi.
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: To Prevent Rabies, Dozens of Semi-Feral Dogs in Mataram Are Targeted for Vaccination.
article.articleSummary: Rabies vaccination campaign targets semi-feral dogs in Mataram City, West Nusa Tenggara (NTB), Indonesia. As of Aug 27, 2026, 87 dogs have been vaccinated across three neighborhoods: Mataram Barat (32), Karang Taliwang (24), and Cilinaya (31). The free program began Aug 25 with ~12 personnel (veterinarians, medical staff, field workers) and aims to reach 100 dogs across four neighborhoods; Cakra Timur is scheduled for Sep 1, 2026. No vaccination refusals reported, and community support is strong, with residents helping capture dogs and handle pets during vaccination. Vaccination days on Aug 28 and Aug 31 were canceled due to preparations for the city’s 33rd anniversary on Aug 31. The initiative focuses on preventing dog-to-human rabies transmission by vaccinating dogs that are owner-leashed but roam at times. Continued outreach and completion of the four-neighborhood target are planned.

triage.headline_ja: 狂犬病予防のため、マタラム市の半野生犬数十頭にワクチン接種を実施
triage.triage_reason: 予防的なワクチン接種活動の通常業務報告であり、異常な症例増加や公衆衛生上の緊急事態を示す情報はない。
triage.notes: 地元自治体による日常的な狂犬病予防ワクチン接種プログラムの進捗報告であり、感染症の異常発生や症例報告は含まれていない。

article.articleHeadline: No new Ebola cases in Uganda for 42 days as Congo toll mounts
article.articleSummary: As of 27 August 2026, Uganda has had no new Ebola cases for 42 days, meeting the WHO threshold to declare the outbreak over there. Uganda's 20 confirmed cases, all traced to a Congo patient, included 2 deaths. In Congo, Ebola has risen, likely circulating undetected since February, with early cases misclassified as malaria. The current outbreak is the Bundibugyo strain, with fewer distinctive symptoms than Zaire. It has spread across six provinces, centered in Ituri in the northeast near Uganda. The Institute of Public Health reports 5,713 confirmed Congo cases and 2,744 deaths; about 770 patients are in treatment or isolation. The outbreak was announced by WHO on May 15.

triage.headline_ja: ウガンダでは42日間新規エボラ症例なし、一方コンゴでは死者数増加
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国で5,713人の確定例、2,744人の死亡という大規模なエボラ出血熱の流行が続いており、既にウガンダへの越境伝播も確認されているため、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する。
triage.notes: ウガンダは対象国リストに含まれないため除外。コンゴでは2月から未検出のまま流行し、初期症例はマラリアと誤診されていた点が異常性・重症度の両面で懸念材料。

article.articleHeadline: Uganda seit 42 Tagen ohne neuen Ebola-Fall, Anstieg im Kongo | Kleine Zeitung
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Uganda: 42 days without a new Ebola case, rise in the Congo | Kleine Zeitung
article.articleSummary: Uganda closes its Ebola outbreak after 42 days with no new cases, marking the end of the Ugandan outbreak after two incubation cycles, according to the WHO Africa Regional Office in Addis Ababa. Uganda has 20 confirmed cases linked to a Congo patient; two deaths. In the Democratic Republic of Congo, Ebola cases have risen since February, now across six provinces with Ituri in the northeast as the hotspot near Uganda. As of 27 August 2026, the DRC reports 5,713 confirmed cases and 2,744 deaths, with about 770 patients in treatment or isolation. The outbreak is caused by Bundibugyo ebolavirus, whose clinical presentation is less conspicuous than Zaire ebolavirus. Initial Congo cases were sometimes misclassified as malaria. The WHO declared the outbreak on 15 May.

triage.headline_ja: ウガンダ、エボラ新規感染42日ゼロ達成、コンゴでは増加
triage.triage_reason: DRCで5,713人の確定患者・2,744人の死亡という大規模アウトブレイクが6州に拡大し、ウガンダへの越境感染も発生しているため、IHR基準複数該当かつ社会的関心も高い。
triage.notes: ウガンダのアウトブレイクは終息と報告されているが、コンゴ（DRC）では感染拡大中であり、対象国リストにはウガンダ・エチオピアが含まれないためDRCのみを検証地域とした。

article.articleHeadline: Lékaři řeší dovolenkové nákazy. Lidé si přivážejí i malárii či horečku dengue
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Doctors are dealing with vacation-related infections. People are bringing back malaria or dengue fever.
article.articleSummary: New pediatric infectious diseases clinic at AGEL Prostějov Hospital in the Olomouc Region reports summer cases of tick-borne illnesses, with Lyme borreliosis rising among children, and increasing mycoplasma infections and parvovirus B19. The unit, the only one of its kind in Olomoucký kraj, treats dozens of pediatric patients weekly; varicella outbreaks occur and collaboration with pediatricians guides hospitalization decisions. Travel-related infections include hepatitis A contracted by an entire family during a vacation in Egypt; measles transmitted to a patient from a brother who travelled to Germany. A 16-year-old from Šternberk diagnosed with dengue after trips to southern Vietnam, with a mild course. In Olomouc FNOL, dengue caused seven hospitalizations and 15 ambulatory cases in four years; eight malaria cases from Sub-Saharan Africa. Authorities warn of a looming autumn COVID wave; vaccination urged, especially for those over 50, covered by insurance. Emphasize hygiene and hydration.

triage.headline_ja: 医師は休暇関連の感染症に対応。人々はマラリアやデング熱を持ち帰ることも
triage.triage_reason: チェコの小児感染症クリニックにおける輸入例（デング熱、マラリア、麻疹、A型肝炎）の散発報告であり、公衆衛生上の深刻な影響や国際的拡大リスクは認められない。
triage.notes: 記事はチェコの病院における輸入感染症（デング熱：ベトナム由来、マラリア：サブサハラアフリカ由来、A型肝炎：エジプト由来、麻疹：ドイツ由来）の個別ケースを報告するもので、対象国での発生事例ではないため verified_locations は空とした。

article.articleHeadline: 15-Year-Old Survives Late-Stage Rabies: How Did the Teen Beat a Nearly Fatal Disease?
article.articleSummary: Rabies in India: A 15-year-old boy from Varanasi, bitten by a stray dog in December 2025, initially received two rabies vaccine doses but later deteriorated. By March 2026 he developed hydrophobia, excessive salivation, and unusual sounds. He was brought to a government health facility in Varanasi, treated for 22 days, and given two additional doses beyond the standard five-dose course, totaling seven injections. The patient subsequently regained consciousness and improved clinically, returning to school. The case is extraordinary but doctors caution against interpreting it as evidence that rabies is curable once symptoms begin. No laboratory confirmation details provided. Infection source: stray dog; no information on ongoing outbreaks or imported/exported cases.

triage.headline_ja: 15歳少年が末期狂犬病から生存：ほぼ致死的な病気にどう打ち勝ったのか
triage.triage_reason: 野良犬による単発の狂犬病症例で、患者の異例の臨床経過に関する医学的関心記事であり、アウトブレイクや公衆衛生上の脅威を示す情報はない。
triage.notes: インドは狂犬病の流行国であり単発症例の生存報告。アウトブレイクや流行拡大の兆候はなく、公衆衛生上の緊急対応を要する情報は含まれていない。対象国リストにインドは含まれるが、本イベントは個別症例の医学的トピックであり感染症危機シグナルとしては該当しないためverified_locationsは空とした。

diseases.name: Human Infection with Swine Influenza A
Human Infection with Swine Influenza A H1N1

article.articleHeadline: स्वाइन फ्लू के बढ़ते मामलों पर ICMR की बड़ी सलाह: किसे कराना चाहिए टेस्ट, कब खत्म होगी संक्रमण की लहर? जानिए सबकुछ
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: ICMR's major advisory on rising swine flu cases: who should get tested, when will the infection wave end? Learn all about it.
article.articleSummary: Swine flu, caused by Influenza A H1N1 pdm09, is spreading across most parts of India, with Delhi among affected areas. Globally, the WHO has declared it a pandemic. The ICMR advises calm, stating most people do not need routine flu testing or vaccination. Testing should be reserved for severe illness or high‑risk groups, including the elderly, the immunocompromised, and pregnant women. Fever can be managed with paracetamol; antivirals such as oseltamivir or antibiotics are not routinely required. Seasonal influenza typically peaks in January–March and late monsoon; the current rise aligns with normal patterns and has not increased mortality. No new H1N1 strain has emerged; the circulating virus remains Influenza A H1N1 pdm09, with Influenza B Victoria lineage also present but not dominant. ICMR surveillance expects cases to stabilize or decline in coming weeks.

triage.headline_ja: スワインフル（豚インフルエンザ）感染増加に関するICMRの重要な助言：誰が検査を受けるべきか、感染の波はいつ終わるのか？すべてを解説
triage.triage_reason: インド国内で豚インフルエンザ（H1N1pdm09）が季節的に増加しているが、ICMRは通常の季節性パターンであり死亡率の増加もなく、新たな変異株も出現していないと明言している。異常性・重症度・国際的拡大のいずれも認められず、社会的関心も高い懸念事案ではないため見送りと判断。
triage.notes: ICMRは季節性インフルエンザの通常範囲内の増加であり、重症化や死亡率上昇は認められないとしている。新規変異株の出現もなく、ルーティンの公衆衛生アドバイザリー的な内容であるため、フルRRAの必要性は低い。

article.articleHeadline: Смертельная вспышка в ДРК: 5713 заражённых Эболой
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Deadly outbreak in the DRC: 5,713 infected with Ebola.
article.articleSummary: An Ebola virus disease outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has reached 5,713 confirmed cases and 2,744 deaths, per the National Institute of Public Health. In the last 24 hours, 57 new cases and 11 deaths were reported. Health workers told the Washington Post that official figures may undercount real infections, with many patients not detected and deaths occurring outside hospitals in Ituri and North Kivu. No vaccine or treatment is licensed for the new Bundibugyo strain, though laboratory data suggest the Ervebo vaccine sent by WHO to DRC may offer some protection. The outbreak continues to spread in eastern provinces amid resource and staff shortages. DRC authorities, with WHO support, are intensifying containment; international bodies urge faster vaccine licensing. The 2018-2020 outbreak killed over 2,000; vaccination helped then, but the current strain appears more resilient. WHO will test cross-strain efficacy of vaccines.

triage.headline_ja: DRCで致死的な感染爆発：エボラ感染者5,713人
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国で新規株（Bundibugyo株）によるエボラ出血熱の大規模流行が発生し、致死率が高く承認済みワクチン・治療薬が存在しないため、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当し国際的関心も高い。
triage.notes: 新規のBundibugyo株によるエボラ流行で、既存ワクチン（Ervebo）の有効性が不明確。医療従事者は実際の感染者数が公式統計より多い可能性を指摘。資源・人員不足により制御が困難な状況。

diseases.name: Human Infection with Swine Influenza A H1N1

article.articleHeadline: Delhi Swine Flu Cases Surge: 138 New H1N1 Infections In 24 Hours, Tally Crosses 2,400
article.articleSummary: Delhi reports 138 new H1N1 cases in 24 hours, taking the 2026 H1N1 tally to 2,446 and total Influenza-A to 3,177. Health Minister Pankaj Kumar Singh held a virtual review to assess bed capacity, testing, medicines and staff, directing at least five isolation beds to be kept free and larger facilities to reserve ten or more beds for influenza and vector-borne disease patients. Compared with the same period in 2025 (229 H1N1 cases), this year’s figures are nearly eightfold higher. H1N1 remains the dominant Influenza-A strain, with H1, H3 and others contributing smaller shares. The rise is attributed to the monsoon season rather than viral mutation. Typical symptoms include fever, cough, sore throat, body aches, chills and fatigue, though fever may be absent. Authorities urge early testing, hygiene, ventilation, and seasonal flu vaccination for high-risk groups; hospitals remain alert through the monsoon.

triage.headline_ja: デリーで豚インフルエンザ感染急増：24時間で138件の新規H1N1感染、累計2,400件超
triage.triage_reason: 季節性インフルエンザ(H1N1)の増加であり、当局は既に対応体制を整えているが、前年比8倍増という異常な増加傾向があるため経過観察が必要。
triage.notes: 既知の季節性インフルエンザ株(H1N1)であり、当局はモンスーン季節の影響と分析。新規変異株ではなく、医療体制も整っているため国際的リスクは低いが、感染者数の急増傾向は注視が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Эпидемия Эболы в Конго может стать крупнейшей в истории
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Ebola epidemic in Congo could be the largest in history.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo (Ituri and North Kivu) is the largest in history, already surpassing the 2018–2022 epidemic (≈2,200 deaths) and spreading faster than the 2014 West Africa outbreak (>11,000 deaths). Officials declared the outbreak in May 2026. It is caused by Bundibugyo ebolavirus, for which there is no vaccine or approved treatment. The World Health Organization warns transmission may have begun as early as February 2026, with Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus stating the outbreak is far from under control. Doctors say official figures likely understate the true scale due to rapid spread and misinformation that deters people from seeking care. Despite the crisis, life in cities continues with large crowds, weddings, and crowded churches. Alis Rib of the International Rescue Committee notes the social backdrop while the epidemic unfolds.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴのエボラ流行、史上最大規模になる可能性
triage.triage_reason: エボラ（ブンディブジョ株）の流行が過去最大規模に拡大し、ワクチン・治療法がなく、WHOも制御下にないと警告しているため、複数のIHR基準・WPRO基準に該当しフルRRAが必要。
triage.notes: ワクチン・承認された治療法がないブンディブジョ株による流行で、WHO事務局長も制御下にないと発言。誤情報により受診が阻害され、実際の規模は過小報告の可能性が指摘されている。

diseases.name: Human Infection with Swine Influenza A H1N1

article.articleHeadline: H1N1 स्वाइन फ्लू का खतरा? घर में होने चाहिए ये गैजेट, कीमत 200 से शुरू
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: H1N1 swine flu risk? These gadgets should be in every home, prices start from ₹200.
article.articleSummary: As of 27 August 2026, Delhi reports 3,000 influenza cases this year, including 2,308 H1N1 infections, with health minister Pankaj Kumar Singh stating sufficient doctors and medicines and that the situation is under control. The article notes ongoing concern about H1N1 transmission in the capital. In response, consumer gadgets are promoted for home protection: pulse oximeters monitor blood oxygen; automatic dispensers to reduce hand contact; UV disinfection lights/boxes claimed to sanitize devices; and digital thermometers to monitor fever. Market listings, including on Amazon, show these devices with prices; automatic dispensers start around ₹800. The piece emphasizes taking precautions at home to detect worsening illness and prevent spread, alongside official assurances of containment in Delhi.

triage.headline_ja: H1N1豚インフルエンザのリスク？家庭に備えるべきガジェット、価格は200ルピーから
triage.triage_reason: デリーでH1N1感染例が2,308件報告されているが、当局は「状況は管理下にある」としており、記事の主目的は消費者向け健康ガジェットの紹介であるため、フルRRAに進むほどの緊急性は認められない。
triage.notes: 季節性H1N1インフルエンザの通常の流行報告であり、当局が管理下にあると明言。記事の主眼は予防用消費者向けガジェットの宣伝で、公衆衛生危機としての新規性は低い。

article.articleHeadline: OMS confirma fim do surto de Ébola no Uganda - O País - A verdade como notícia
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: WHO confirms end of the Ebola outbreak in Uganda - O País - The truth as news.
article.articleSummary: WHO confirmed the end of the Ebola outbreak in Uganda after 42 days without new cases following the last confirmed patient. Uganda had declared the outbreak over last month, but WHO maintained surveillance to ensure no new transmission chains. Since May 15, when neighboring Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) announced a new Ebola outbreak, Uganda reported 20 cases, all linked to the DRC outbreak, with initial infections in Uganda acquired from travelers from Congo before diagnosis. Preventive measures included canceling large events, discouraging handshakes, and suspending transport and flights between Uganda and the DRC. The situation remains dire in eastern DRC, where the Bundibugyo strain has caused over 4,500 confirmed cases in six provinces and more than 2,000 deaths, with no vaccine or approved treatment. WHO warned cross-border spread remains high and updated recommendations emphasize surveillance, case detection/investigation, prevention, and community engagement, while maintaining regional alert.

triage.headline_ja: WHO、ウガンダでのエボラ出血熱流行終息を確認
triage.triage_reason: ウガンダの流行は終息したが、隣接するDRCでは同系統(ブンディブギョ株)の流行が継続し4,500例以上・死者2,000人超と深刻で、越境拡大リスクが高いまま維持されているため、フルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: 記事の主題はウガンダの流行終息宣言だが、感染源であり現在も進行中の深刻な流行地はDRC東部。ウガンダはBluedotの発生地域に含まれるが対象国リストに存在しないため verified_locations から除外。

article.articleHeadline: Quezon logs 2,276 cases, 12 deaths from January to August
article.articleSummary: Quezon province, Philippines, reported 2,276 dengue cases and 12 deaths from January to August 22 this year, a 38% reduction versus 2025, according to the Quezon Provincial Health Office. Of the 2,276 cases, 1,018 were suspected, 467 probable, and 791 confirmed dengue infections. Mauban municipality recorded the highest burden with 406 cases and four deaths. Children aged 1 to 10 accounted for 38% of total cases, and 46% showed warning signs of severe dengue. Dengue is transmitted by infected Aedes mosquitoes; common symptoms include high fever, severe headache, pain behind the eyes, muscle and joint pains, nausea, vomiting, fatigue, and skin rashes. Severe dengue can cause persistent vomiting, severe abdominal pain, bleeding, and breathing difficulties. Authorities stress early diagnosis and prompt treatment to prevent severe complications and deaths.

triage.headline_ja: ケソン州、1月から8月までにデング熱2,276例、死亡12例を記録
triage.triage_reason: フィリピン・ケソン州のデング熱は前年比38%減少しており、地域的な流行病の定例報告に過ぎず、異常性・国際的拡大リスク・社会的関心の高まりは認められない。
triage.notes: デング熱はフィリピンの地域的流行病であり、本記事は前年比減少を報告する定例的な公衆衛生統計。特別な対応や外部支援の必要性は示されていない。

article.articleHeadline: হু হু করে বাড়ছে আক্রান্ত ও মৃত্যুর সংখ্যা: কঙ্গোয় ইতিহাসের ভয়াবহতম ইবোলা প্রাদুর্ভাবের আশঙ্কা
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The number of cases and deaths is rising rapidly: Congo fears the most devastating Ebola outbreak in history.
article.articleSummary: As of August 27, 2026, the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) has entered a highly alarming phase, with Ituri province's capital Bunia identified as the outbreak's epicenter. Official figures from the DRC health ministry report 5,584 infections and 2,680 deaths, though doctors in affected areas say the true toll is much higher. The crisis has prompted warnings that it could become the most devastating Ebola outbreak in history, surpassing the 2014 West Africa epidemic. The outbreak began on May 15, simultaneously in DRC and neighboring Uganda, where authorities declared Uganda Ebola-free on July 28. Six DRC provinces are now affected. Critical response constraints include insufficient funding and resources after aid cuts from the US and other Western nations, hampering case finding, surveillance, quarantine, and essential medical supplies. Public gatherings and celebrations risk accelerating transmission.

triage.headline_ja: 感染者・死者数が急増中：コンゴで史上最悪のエボラ流行の恐れ
triage.triage_reason: DRCで感染者5,584人・死者2,680人と急拡大し、史上最悪のエボラ流行になる恐れがあり、複数州に拡大、国際支援不足も指摘されているためフルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: ウガンダは記事中で発生国として言及されているが、7月28日にエボラ終息宣言済みかつ対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations には含めない。米国等西側諸国からの資金・資源削減が対応の障害となっている点は特筆事項。

article.articleHeadline: Kabus geri döndü: Salgın 3 ülkeye sıçradı, hızla yayılıyor
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Nightmare Is Back: The Outbreak Has Spread to Three Countries and Is Spreading Rapidly.
article.articleSummary: Monkeypox (mpox) outbreak first detected in Guinea-Bissau has spread to three countries and is spreading rapidly. Globally since 2022, mpox has caused about 190,000 laboratory-confirmed cases in 145 countries. In Guinea-Bissau, UNICEF reports 46 suspected cases, with 23 under 15 years old and many under four, highlighting pediatric vulnerability amid constrained health resources. Mpox features fever, chills, muscle aches, and vesicular rash, and transmits through close contact; experts warn that crowded settings and displaced populations in West Africa heighten transmission risk. Two WHO-recommended vaccines exist, but supply gaps persist, delaying protection in low-income settings; a forthcoming global stockpile aims to accelerate distribution. In the Democratic Republic of the Congo, a faster-spreading Clade I variant emerged in 2024. The antiviral tecovirimat showed no clear advantage over placebo, underscoring that early diagnosis, contact tracing, supportive care, vaccination where feasible, and robust public health surveillance remain vital.

triage.headline_ja: 悪夢が再来：アウトブレイクが3カ国に拡大、急速に広がる
triage.triage_reason: Mpox（特にDRCで確認された急速拡大するClade I変異株）が複数国に拡大しており、IHR基準の複数項目（深刻性・異常性・国際的拡大）に該当するためフルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: 記事はギニアビサウ発のアウトブレイクが3カ国（ギニアビサウ、DRC、アンゴラ）へ拡大したと報じているが、対象国リストに該当するのはDRCのみ。DRCでは急速に拡大するClade I変異株が2024年に出現しており、特に注視が必要。ギニアビサウでは小児への影響が顕著（46疑い例中23例が15歳未満）だが対象国外のため verified_locations には含めない。

article.articleHeadline: 호수에서 물놀이 후 8세 여아 사망... '뇌 먹는 아메바' 공포
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: An 8-year-old girl dies after playing in a lake... 'brain-eating amoeba' fear.
article.articleSummary: An eight-year-old girl, Lilian Smart, died in Louisiana from Naegleria fowleri infection contracted while swimming in Claybon Lake. She developed fever, was hospitalized, and sustained severe brain damage, dying about eight days after onset. Naegleria fowleri causes Primary Amoebic Meningoencephalitis; infection occurs when warm freshwater enters the nasal passages, reaching the brain via the olfactory nerve. There is no transmission through drinking water and no human-to-human spread. From 1937–2025, roughly 180 US cases have been confirmed, with a case fatality around 97%. Prevention emphasizes avoiding swimming in warm lakes, rivers, and reservoirs during hot weather, not submerging the head, using nose clips, and ensuring well-maintained, chlorinated pools. For nasal exposure, boiled and cooled water or sterile saline should be used. Warming waters may expand the amoeba’s habitat northward; Korea reported one imported case in 2022 (a stay in Thailand), and cases have occurred in Japan and Taiwan.

triage.headline_ja: 湖で水遊びをした後、8歳の女児が死亡...「脳を食べるアメーバ」への恐怖
triage.triage_reason: 米国ルイジアナ州における単発のネグレリア・フォーレリ感染死亡例であり、ヒト-ヒト感染なし、既知の病原体・感染経路であるため異常性は低く、対象国での発生も確認されない。
triage.notes: 記事の主題は米国ルイジアナ州での単発死亡例。タイ・韓国・日本・台湾への言及は過去の輸入例や気候変動による分布拡大の可能性についての一般的言及であり、対象国での実際の発生ではないためverified_locationsには含めない。

article.articleHeadline: Capitol steps up drive against leptospirosis
article.articleSummary: As of August 27, 2026, Pampanga province, Philippines, is intensifying surveillance for leptospirosis, influenza, and dengue alongside other water-borne illnesses in response to flooding. Gov. Lilia Pineda and Vice Gov. Dennis Pineda, with the Provincial Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office and Provincial Health Office, are visiting affected communities in Apalit, Macabebe, Masantol, City of San Fernando, Minalin, and Sto. Tomas to provide assistance, medicines, and safety reminders. A health lecture was conducted; thousands of doxycycline doses have been distributed as post-exposure preventive treatment for those at risk from floodwater. Leptospirosis testing kits will be provided to district hospitals to bolster monitoring of suspected cases. Residents are urged to seek medical care for fever, body pain, weakness, or other symptoms after wading through floodwater.

triage.headline_ja: 州庁、レプトスピラ症対策の取り組みを強化
triage.triage_reason: 洪水後の水系感染症（レプトスピラ症・インフルエンザ・デング熱）に対する予防的サーベイランス強化の報道であり、現時点で重大な公衆衛生上の異常事態や国際的拡大の兆候は確認されないが、今後の症例動向を注視する必要がある。
triage.notes: 洪水後の季節性・環境性感染症対策としての予防的措置であり、地方自治体主導で管理可能。感染者数や重症度に関する具体的データは記事内に記載なし。

article.articleHeadline: Ελληνική ερευνητική ομάδα αναπτύσσει rapid test για τον ιό του Δυτικού Νείλου - dete.gr
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Greek research team develops a rapid test for the West Nile virus - dete.gr
article.articleSummary: Greek researchers from the National and Kapodistrian University of Athens are developing a rapid, point-of-care test that uses a single drop of blood to detect West Nile virus (WNV) and three other mosquito-borne pathogens—Zika, dengue fever, and chikungunya—via a portable device employing graphene biosensors. Part of the SURVIVE-VBD EU4Health project with a 4 million euro budget, the effort also involves Italy, Spain, Estonia, the Netherlands, and Brazil, led by Maria Gazouli. The work addresses rising WNV activity in Greece amid climate change and expanding mosquito vectors. Greece has no domestic Zika, dengue, or chikungunya cases to date, only imported ones, though European vectors exist. An AI model will couple test results with environmental data to map high-risk areas and issue alerts. Timeline: 36 months; successful development could enable preventive screening by Mobile Health Teams and bolster surveillance.

triage.headline_ja: ギリシャの研究チームが西ナイル熱ウイルスの迅速検査法を開発 - dete.gr
triage.triage_reason: 研究開発（迅速検査ツール）に関する記事であり、実際の感染症アウトブレイクを報告するものではない。対象国での発生事例もない。
triage.notes: 記事はギリシャ・EU諸国（イタリア、スペイン、エストニア、オランダ、ブラジル）が参加する研究プロジェクト（SURVIVE-VBD）に関するもので、感染症発生地はギリシャであり対象国リストに含まれない。ブラジルは研究協力国として言及されているが、感染症発生国としての言及ではないため除外。

article.articleHeadline: Έρχεται rapid τεστ για τον ιό του Δυτικού Νείλου - Η Ελληνίδα επικεφαλής μιλά στο ygeiamou.gr - Mesogeios TV
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: A rapid test for the West Nile virus is coming - The Greek head speaks to ygeiamou.gr - Mesogeios TV
article.articleSummary: Rapid test for West Nile virus and three additional viruses is being studied by the University of Athens as part of the EU SURVIVE-VBD project, funded by EU4Health with a total budget of 4 million euros. The test uses a single drop of blood to detect West Nile virus and three other viruses. This summer, West Nile virus shows extensive spread in Greece, with markedly higher numbers of cases and deaths than in previous years. Mosquito populations—expanded by climate change—are rising across Europe, enabling transmission of serious diseases such as dengue fever. The EU has invited participation in SURVIVE-VBD, a multinational project involving Greece, Italy, Spain, Estonia, the Netherlands, and Brazil. Greece's team is led by Professor Maria Gazouli of the University of Athens (Biology, Genetics, Nanomedicine).

triage.headline_ja: 西ナイルウイルスの迅速検査が登場へ - ギリシャの研究責任者がygeiamou.grに語る
triage.triage_reason: 記事はEUの研究プロジェクト（SURVIVE-VBD）に関する内容で、ギリシャでの西ナイル熱拡大が主題。ブラジルは共同研究参加国として名前が挙がっているのみで、実際の疾病発生国ではないため対象外。
triage.notes: 記事の主題はEU研究プロジェクト（迅速検査開発）であり、対象国リストにあるブラジルは共同研究参加国として名前が挙がっているだけで、実際の感染症発生国はギリシャ（対象国外）である。

article.articleHeadline: Delhi H1N1 cases cross 2,600 as 166 new cases reported in 24 hours
article.articleSummary: Delhi reports 166 new H1N1 cases in the last 24 hours, taking the total to over 2,600. The rise accompanies an uptick in respiratory illnesses in the city. Health Minister Dr Pankaj Singh visited Indira Gandhi Hospital to review preparedness and arrangements to manage influenza and respiratory illness cases. The government is monitoring the situation and reviewing hospital preparedness across Delhi. Dr Singh said there is no need to panic, urging caution and basic precautions. H1N1 influenza spreads mainly via coughing or sneezing; common symptoms include fever, cough, sore throat, body aches, headache, fatigue, and sometimes breathing difficulties. Preventive measures include hand hygiene, covering mouth and nose while coughing or sneezing, avoiding close contact with the unwell, and seeking medical advice if symptoms worsen.

triage.notes: 季節性インフルエンザ(H1N1)の症例増加であり、デリー保健当局が病院の準備状況を確認している。重症度や死亡率に関する情報がなく、パニックの必要はないとされている。

article.articleHeadline: H1N1 Cases Rise As Heavy Rains Batter India: What This Double Trouble Means For Travellers
article.articleSummary: Heavy monsoon rains and rising H1N1 influenza cases are disrupting travel across India, with Delhi issuing an IMD red alert on Aug 24 for waterlogging and flight cancellations on Aug 25 to Leh, Ayodhya, Srinagar, Dharamshala, Mumbai and Cochin. H1N1 and Influenza-A activity is surging: Delhi reports over 2,400 H1N1 and more than 3,100 Influenza-A; Karnataka records 4,212 lab-confirmed influenza cases by Aug 22; Kerala reports 7,421 infections and 88 deaths; spikes are also noted in Maharashtra, Mumbai and West Bengal. Transmission is via respiratory droplets in crowded, poorly ventilated spaces such as airports and rail stations. No new H1N1 strain has been identified; the rise aligns with a seasonal monsoon linked pattern. Travelers should use precautions: masks (optional in many settings), hand hygiene, rest if ill, and annual influenza vaccination. Symptoms include fever, cough, sore throat, body aches, headache, chills and fatigue.

triage.headline_ja: H1N1感染例が増加、インドを襲う大雨との「二重の困難」——旅行者への影響とは
triage.triage_reason: 季節性インフルエンザ（新規株なし）だが、ケララ州で7421例・88死亡、カルナタカ州で4212例確認など複数州で急増しており、重症度・流行しやすさの基準に該当。旅行への影響（フライト運休）を伴い社会的関心も高い。
triage.notes: 記事は新規H1N1株の出現ではなく、季節性（モンスーン関連）のインフルエンザ増加と明記。ただし複数州（デリー、カルナタカ、ケララ、マハラシュトラ、西ベンガル）で感染者数増加および死亡例が報告されており、公衆衛生上の負荷増大が懸念される。渡航制限は大雨による交通障害が主因でH1N1自体による制限ではない。

article.articleHeadline: US issues guidance on travellers denied boarding a flight over Ebola-related restrictions
article.articleSummary: Ebola-related flight restrictions tied to the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) outbreak are in effect. Anyone physically present in the DRC within 21 days of a scheduled US-bound flight is barred from boarding, regardless of citizenship. In addition, foreign nationals and US lawful permanent residents who have been in Uganda or South Sudan are barred from US flights until 21 days after leaving those countries. Travellers who have been in Uganda or South Sudan but not the DRC may fly to the United States, but must enter through Washington Dulles, Atlanta, Houston, or New York's JFK. Affected travellers should email Ebola-Travel-HELP@hq.dhs.gov with full name, date of birth, passport details, current location, and flight information; automated replies may occur, followed by a response by phone or a verified .gov address. For emergency lodging or consular services, contact the nearest U.S. embassy or consulate.

triage.headline_ja: 米国、エボラ関連の渡航制限により搭乗を拒否された旅行者向けのガイダンスを発表
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国(DRC)のエボラ流行に伴い米国が渡航制限措置を実施しており、IHR基準（重大な公衆衛生影響、国際的拡大リスク、渡航制限）に複数該当するためフルリスク評価に進むべき。
triage.notes: 記事はDRCで発生中のエボラ流行を受けた米国の渡航制限・搭乗拒否対応に関するもの。ウガンダ・南スーダンも渡航制限対象だが対象国リストに含まれないため除外。米国自体も対象国外のため除外。

article.articleHeadline: 虫媒传染病防控不力！大朗2家诊所被立案查处
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Inadequate prevention and control of vector-borne infectious diseases! Two clinics in Dalang have been put under investigation.
article.articleSummary: During dengue fever and chikungunya season in Dalang Town, Dongguan, authorities and the town health bureau conducted infectious disease prevention inspections at local clinics. Two clinics were found to record only basic patient details (name, gender, address, phone, treatment) and failed to log recent travel history and body temperature, signaling noncompliance with mandatory prevention and control duties. These clinics have been placed under investigation. Under Chinese law, medical institutions that do not fulfill prevention responsibilities can face penalties up to 100,000 yuan, with possible license suspension for serious cases. Officials warn that missing registration items create vulnerabilities in epidemic tracing. Dalang’s vector-borne disease control command will enforce pre-examination, triage, and complete, traceable patient information. The town will maintain ongoing daily inspections and joint enforcement with zero tolerance for lapses, reinforcing the public health safety net.

triage.headline_ja: 媒介動物由来感染症の防疫不十分！大朗の診療所2軒が調査対象に
triage.triage_reason: デング熱・チクングニア熱の流行期における診療所の記録不備に関する行政処分の記事であり、具体的な症例数や重症度の情報がなく、感染状況の実態は不明なため続報を注視する。
triage.notes: 記事は東莞市大朗鎮でのデング熱・チクングニア熱流行期における診療所の防疫記録不備に対する行政処分に関する内容で、実際の感染者数や重症度データは記載されていない。

article.articleHeadline: Ituri : rentrée scolaire maintenue au 1er septembre, les acteurs éducatifs formés contre Ebola
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ituri: School year starts on September 1; educators trained against Ebola.
article.articleSummary: Ituri authorities will open the 2026-2027 school year on Tuesday, September 1, 2026, despite concerns over the Ebola virus disease outbreak in the province. A two-day capacity-building workshop in Bunia trained 50 inspectors, senior educational staff, and representatives from ANAPECO and ASONEPA on Ebola prevention and protection in schools; together with similar sessions in Ituri 2 and Ituri 3, the program totals 150 trainers province-wide. Trained actors will cascade lessons to school directors, teachers, and parent committees to establish a prevention chain from officials to students and families. The initiative, supported financially and logistically by Incident Management of the Ebola response with STAR-RDC, aims to reinforce handwashing and other protective measures. Despite calls to postpone, PROVED interim confirms the start with strengthened school health measures, seeking to maintain education while safeguarding health.

triage.headline_ja: イツリ州：9月1日に新学期開始を維持、教育関係者にエボラ対策研修を実施
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国イツリ州で進行中のエボラ出血熱流行に関連する記事であり、IHR基準・WPRO基準の複数に該当するため、既存流行の状況確認としてフルRRA相当の注視が必要。
triage.notes: 本記事自体は新規感染例の報告ではなく、既存のエボラ流行下での学校再開に伴う予防研修に関する内容。しかしエボラという疾患の性質上、公衆衛生上の重大性・国際的拡散リスクが高く、既存流行の継続状況として注視が必要。

article.articleHeadline: 5 ที่ตรวจโควิดและไข้หวัดใหญ่ รู้ให้ชัดว่าป่วยอะไร อ่านผลไว สั่งออนไลน์ได้เลย
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: 5 Places to Get Tested for COVID and Influenza: Know Exactly What You're Ill With, Get Results Fast, and Order Online Now
article.articleSummary: A Thai consumer guide highlights multiplex rapid antigen tests that detect SARS-CoV-2 (COVID-19) and influenza A/B simultaneously, with some 4-in-1 or 5-in-1 kits also covering RSV and Adenovirus. This is motivated by COVID-19 now being endemic and symptoms overlapping with influenza (fever, cough, sore throat, body aches). Notable products include Wilbur’s 3–9 in 1 kits (one test per box; results in about 15 minutes), GICA Testsealabs FLU A/B+ Covid-19 3-in-1 (nasal swab; 10–15 minutes), Fanttest 2-in-1 (COVID + Flu A/B), Nexgen 4-in-1 (COVID, RSV, Flu A/B; nasal swab; read in 10 minutes; imported from the United States), and Reagen 4-in-1 (COVID, Flu A/B, RSV; 15 minutes). Results use C and T lines: one C line = negative; C and T (or faint T) = positive; three cases deemed invalid, retest with a new kit. Positive results prompt isolation; negative cases with symptoms should mask and monitor with retesting as needed.

triage.headline_ja: 5つのCOVID・インフルエンザ検査キット紹介：何の病気か正確に把握、迅速判定、オンライン注文も可能
triage.triage_reason: 本記事は消費者向け検査キットの紹介であり、疾病の発生や流行を報じるものではないため、シグナルとしての該当性がない。
triage.notes: 記事は検査キットの製品紹介・購入案内であり、タイ国内での具体的な感染症発生・流行状況の報告ではない。

article.articleHeadline: 母胎單身22年嫁初戀！妹子崩潰婚檢「驗出愛滋陽性」　醫追生活史未婚夫聽懵了
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: A 22-year-old who has never dated marries her first love! The bride collapses at the premarital medical exam after testing HIV-positive; the doctor traces her medical history, and the fiancé is stunned.
article.articleSummary: In Anhui Province, China, a 22-year-old woman (pseudonym Wanwan) who had never dated until university tested HIV antibody-positive during a premarital medical examination, shocking her fiancé. Doctors reviewed her past life history and traced the infection’s possible origin; she recalled having her ears pierced in a shop in an urban village. While this raises concerns about exposure to contaminated needles, experts say a single ear piercing cannot confirm the infection route, which requires laboratory confirmation. The report highlights bloodborne infection risks linked to cosmetic procedures when instruments are not properly sterilized or replaced, with potential HIV, hepatitis B, and hepatitis C transmission. The case emphasizes safe piercing practices and the importance of premarital screening; no other cases or outcomes are reported.

triage.headline_ja: 22年間彼氏なしの女性が初恋の人と結婚へ！婚前検査で『HIV陽性』判明、医師が生活歴を調査し婚約者は困惑

triage.notes: 単一症例の報道であり、感染経路も未確定。美容施術における感染管理の注意喚起的な記事であり、公衆衛生上の緊急性は認められない。

article.articleHeadline: Delhi H1N1 Surge: Cases To Dip Post-Monsoon, Says Health Minister Dr Pankaj Kumar Singh
article.articleSummary: Delhi records a surge in H1N1 (swine flu) during the monsoon, with 138 new cases in the last 24 hours and a year-to-date total of 2,446; Influenza-A cases in the capital reach 3,177. Officials attribute the rise to seasonal changes and high humidity in the National Capital Delhi and surrounding areas, prompting a high-alert response. Health Minister Dr Pankaj Kumar Singh chaired reviews with the health department, municipal corporations and major hospitals, directing strengthened emergency services and expanded isolation beds, doctors, testing facilities, essential medicines, and other critical resources. He cautioned against panic, stating H1N1 is seasonal and will subside after the monsoon. Most patients present with fever and flu-like symptoms and are discharged within one to two days after primary treatment. Dedicated isolation rooms and beds have been prepared across hospitals to prevent further spread.

triage.headline_ja: デリーでH1N1感染急増：季節性で雨季後には減少するとパンカジ・クマール・シン保健大臣が発言
triage.triage_reason: 季節性インフルエンザ(H1N1)の増加であり異常性は低いが、症例数の急増と保健当局の高度警戒対応が見られるため継続監視が望ましい。
triage.notes: 季節性インフルエンザ(H1N1)の毎年繰り返される流行パターンであり、患者の大半は軽症で1-2日で退院。保健省は季節変化とモンスーン後の減少を予測しており、パンデミック相当の異常事象とは言えない。ただし症例数（24時間で138件、累計2,446件）と行政の対応強化の動きは注視に値する。

article.articleHeadline: Bali plays down Zika concerns after US issues travel health warning
article.articleSummary: Bali, Indonesia reports no confirmed Zika cases, even as the CDC issues a Level 2 travel health notice citing rising Zika among travelers returning from Bali. Bali Health Agency head I Nyoman Gede Anom said surveillance found no cases and described warning as an early signal to strengthen surveillance and preparedness. Authorities will bolster entry-point monitoring (airports, seaports) and urge healthcare workers to detect Zika symptoms—fever, rash, red eyes, muscle and joint pain, headache. The Health Ministry plans to expand laboratory capacity and enhance surveillance for Zika and other mosquito-borne viruses for diagnosis. Residents and travelers are urged to maintain cleanliness and seek care if symptomatic. CDC advises precautions against mosquito bites and sexual transmission; pregnant travelers should avoid Bali and delay pregnancy after travel. Zika is transmitted by Aedes mosquitoes; no vaccine or specific treatment; microcephaly risk. As of 2026, WHO reports Zika transmission in 97 countries, including Indonesia.

triage.headline_ja: バリ島、米国の渡航健康警告発令後、ジカ熱への懸念を軽視
triage.triage_reason: 米CDCがバリ島からの帰国者にジカ熱増加を理由に渡航健康警告（レベル2）を発出し、妊婦への渡航自粛勧告も出されたことで国際的拡大・渡航制限の基準に該当する一方、現地当局は感染確認例なしとしており情報に矛盾があるため注視が必要。
triage.notes: 現地バリ保健当局は確認症例なしと主張しているが、米CDCは帰国旅行者の症例増加を根拠に渡航警告を発出しており、サーベイランス体制の齟齬が懸念される。続報でのラボ確認結果の有無を要確認。

article.articleHeadline: AI membaca rontgen, memburu TBC sebelum terlambat
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: AI reads X-ray images to detect TB before it's too late.
article.articleSummary: Indonesia accounts for about 10% of global tuberculosis (TB) cases in 2024, second to India, with WHO estimating ~1.09 million Indonesians with TB in 2023 and an incidence of 387–388 per 100,000. In Jakarta, TBScreen.AI, a computer-aided detection system for chest X-rays developed by Universitas Gadjah Mada (UGM) and partners, screens for TB by highlighting radiographic shadows to prioritize further testing; it is not a diagnosis. In August 2026, TBScreen.AI showed sensitivity ~83% and specificity ~87%, promising for screening but requiring external multisite validation before wide-scale use. Prison settings illustrate active-case finding challenges: 2023 saw 6,039 TB diagnoses via screening; 2024 detection fell with symptom-based screening; 2025, broader X-ray screening identified 7,972 cases. Yearly case counts reflect screening coverage and methods, not direct incidence shifts, underscoring the need to translate detection into diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of transmission.

triage.headline_ja: AIがレントゲン画像を読み取り、手遅れになる前に結核を検出
triage.triage_reason: 本記事はインドネシアにおける結核（既知の常在流行病）のAIスクリーニング技術に関する報道であり、急性の異常発生や新興感染症イベントではないため、シグナルトリアージの対象とはしない。
triage.notes: 記事はインドネシアの結核（TB）常在流行の負担とAIを用いた胸部X線スクリーニング技術（TBScreen.AI）の性能評価に関する内容。インドはWHO統計上の比較対象国として言及されているのみで、実際のイベント発生国ではないため verified_locations から除外した。

article.articleHeadline: African Vaccine Candidate For Bundibugyo Ebola For Clinical Trials -CEPI - News Agency Of Nigeria
article.articleSummary: Minapharm Group, via its Berlin-based ProBioGen subsidiary, secured about $16.5 million from CEPI to advance a Bundibugyo ebolavirus vaccine candidate into preclinical development and an early-stage Phase 1 trial in Africa. The vaccine uses ProBioGen's MVA-CR19 platform—a highly attenuated, replication-deficient modified vaccinia Ankara vector delivering antigens to elicit B- and T-cell responses for broader and longer-lasting immunity. The program addresses the Democratic Republic of the Congo's (DRC) largest Bundibugyo-driven Ebola outbreak on record. If Phase 1 is successful, CEPI envisages later-stage trials to support Emergency Use Authorisation and WHO prequalification; CEPI has already funded four other Bundibugyo candidates, with Minapharm's as the fifth. GMP drug substance will be produced at ProBioGen's Germany facility and shipped to Minapharm's Cairo site for formulation, with a planned transfer to Cairo to enable local manufacturing. This aligns with Africa CDC's emphasis on building regional vaccine capacity.

triage.headline_ja: アフリカ発のブンディブギョ・エボラ用ワクチン候補、臨床試験へ ―CEPI
triage.triage_reason: 本記事はワクチン開発資金提供に関する報道であり、新規の発生・拡大に関する疫学的情報は含まれていない。既知のDRCアウトブレイクに言及するのみで、新たなシグナルとしての価値は低い。
triage.notes: 記事はCEPI資金によるBundibugyo型エボラワクチン(MVA-CR19)の第I相試験開始に関する内容。DRCの「史上最大のBundibugyo型アウトブレイク」との言及があるが、これは既存の発生に対する背景説明であり、本記事自体は新規の公衆衛生イベントの発生や拡大を報告するものではない。既存アウトブレイクの動向は別途モニタリングが必要。

article.articleHeadline: H1N1 Virus Alert: किन लोगों को स्वाइन फ्लू में ICU तक पहुंचने का खतरा ज्यादा? डॉक्टर ने बताए 5 बड़े कारण
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: H1N1 Virus Alert: Which people are at higher risk of ICU admission due to swine flu? The doctor has listed five major reasons.
article.articleSummary: As of August 27, 2026, Delhi and several states report rising H1N1 (Swine Flu) cases. While most infections resolve, some progress to severe disease requiring ICU care. Dr. Neeraj Kumar of Sharda Care-HealthCity notes five major risk factors and warning signs. High-risk groups include people with diabetes or heart, kidney, or liver disease; those with weakened immunity; pregnant women; and both young children and the elderly. The illness can rapidly deteriorate when pre-existing conditions exist or when treatment is delayed. Early symptoms resemble a mild viral illness, but respiratory distress and falling oxygen levels signal severe disease, potentially necessitating hospitalization, ventilation, and intensive care. Delay in seeking care—mistaking early symptoms for a routine fever—greatly increases risk of pneumonia and complications. Early medical evaluation and swine flu treatment are emphasized to reduce ICU admissions.

triage.headline_ja: H1N1ウイルス警報：スワインフルーでICU入院のリスクが高いのはどんな人か？医師が5つの主要因を解説
triage.triage_reason: デリー等でH1N1患者数増加が報告されているが、これは季節性インフルエンザに関する注意喚起・医療情報記事であり、規模や深刻度に関する具体的データが不足している。
triage.notes: 記事は医師によるリスク因子解説が中心で、感染規模・死亡者数などの具体的疫学データは記載されていない。H1N1はインドで季節的に流行しており、今回の報告が異常な事象かどうかは不明。

article.articleHeadline: Medical Shortages, Monsoon Illnesses Put More Than 600 IDPs at Risk in Western Pai Khun - Shan Herald Agency for News
article.articleSummary: More than 600 internally displaced people (IDPs) in Lar Tein Village, western Pai Khun (Pekhon) Township, face a healthcare crisis as seasonal flu and fevers spread during the monsoon, amid a regime blockade on medical supplies. Displaced from Baw Yan, Taung Hsa Long and Myauk Hsa Long villages since September 2025, they have endured nearly 11 months of displacement. Remote, mountainous terrain and damaged roads hinder transport of medicines, and regime restrictions on basic goods worsen shortages. Local resistance medics provide care but cannot meet demand. Medicines are urgently needed, especially for flu and malaria. Across western Pai Khun, more than 6,000 people from about 10 villages remain displaced, sheltering in forests and host communities with little access to humanitarian assistance.

triage.headline_ja: 医療物資不足とモンスーン期の疾病により、パイクン西部の600人以上のIDPが危険に晒される - シャン・ヘラルド通信
triage.triage_reason: ミャンマー国内避難民キャンプでインフルエンザ・マラリアが流行し医療支援が不足しているが、重症度や感染規模の詳細データが不明であり、局地的な人道危機としての側面が強いため経過観察とする。
triage.notes: 軍政による医療物資封鎖と紛争由来の避難生活が背景。感染症そのものよりも人道支援アクセスの欠如が主要な問題であり、疾病の重症度・拡大範囲の続報を要する。

article.articleHeadline: Há risco de sarampo em Portugal? DGS confirma nove casos este ano, três importados - 24 Notícias
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Is there a risk of measles in Portugal? DGS confirms nine cases this year, three imported - 24 Notícias.
article.articleSummary: Portugal has recorded nine measles cases in 2026 through 18 August, including three imported and three locally acquired; the origins of the remaining three are under investigation. A three-case transmission chain is identified and controlled, while other origins are still being analyzed. The DGS notes that international circulation of measles does not automatically imply sustained transmission in Portugal. The Brazil outbreak in São Paulo is ongoing, with authorities boosting vaccination in three municipalities. Cross-border movement is substantial, with 534,379 Brazilian guests staying in Portugal’s tourist accommodations January–June 2026. Vaccination remains a key barrier, with 95.7% of six-year-olds vaccinated against measles, mumps and rubella in 2024. The DGS advises travelers to affected areas to have up-to-date measles vaccination and to check vaccine records, especially for young children, while maintaining epidemiological and laboratory surveillance.

triage.headline_ja: ポルトガルで麻疹のリスクはあるか？DGSが今年9例（輸入例3件を含む）を確認 - 24 Notícias
triage.triage_reason: ブラジル（サンパウロ）で麻疹アウトブレイクが進行中であり、渡航者数が多いポルトガルへの輸入例発生とヒトヒト感染の可能性があるため、スクリーニング基準に複数該当し社会的関心も認められる。
triage.notes: 記事の主題はポルトガルの麻疹輸入例だが、対象国リストにポルトガルは含まれないため除外。ブラジル・サンパウロでの麻疹アウトブレイクが継続中との具体的記述があるため、対象国のブラジルのみverified_locationsに含めた。

article.articleHeadline: दिल्ली में H1N1 के केस 2600 पार, बढ़ते स्वाइन फ्लू के बीच अस्पतालों की तैयारियां तेज
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: H1N1 cases in Delhi cross 2,600 as swine flu rises; hospitals gear up.
article.articleSummary: H1N1 (swine flu) cases in Delhi surpass 2,600 with 166 new infections reported in the last 24 hours. Delhi government is reviewing hospital preparedness as the surge continues; Health Minister Dr. Pankaj Singh visited Indira Gandhi Hospital to assess facilities, resources, and capacity to handle an increasing patient load. Authorities are instructing hospitals to remain alert and strengthen arrangements to ensure adequate beds, medications, and staff. Public guidance emphasizes caution, not panic; health professionals urge prompt medical consultation for flu-like symptoms—fever, cough, sore throat, or breathing difficulties—and adherence to general infection-prevention measures in crowded places. ICMR notes that the rising cases are not due to a new H1N1 strain but are linked to seasonal influenza. Efforts center on timely treatment and disseminating accurate information to the public.

triage.headline_ja: デリーでH1N1（豚インフルエンザ）感染者数が2600人を超え、増加する中で病院側の対応が加速
triage.triage_reason: デリーでH1N1感染者が急増し病院が対応を強化しているが、ICMRは新型株ではなく季節性インフルエンザと説明。国内の社会的・行政的関心が高く、WPRO基準（持続的曝露・流行しやすさ）にも該当するためフルRRAでの確認が望ましい。
triage.notes: ICMRは今回の増加が新型H1N1株によるものではなく季節性インフルエンザに関連すると説明しており、異常性は低いと判断される。ただし感染者数の急増と病院対応の強化から継続的な監視が必要。

article.articleHeadline: أوغندا لم تسجل أي إصابة جديدة بإيبولا منذ 42 يوما فيما ترتفع الحصيلة في الكونغو - بوابة الشروق
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Uganda has not recorded any new Ebola cases in the last 42 days, while the tally rises in Congo.
article.articleSummary: Uganda declares the end of its Ebola outbreak after 42 days with no new cases; all 20 confirmed cases were linked to an index patient who arrived from Congo, with 2 deaths. The Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) continues to report rising infections, with the outbreak begun on May 15 and now spreading across six provinces, centered in Ituri province near the Uganda border. The current outbreak is caused by Bundibugyo ebolavirus, which often presents with less distinctive symptoms than the Zaire strain. According to the Institute of Public Health, 5,713 confirmed cases and 2,744 deaths have been recorded overall in the DRC, with about 770 patients currently being treated or isolated. The World Health Organization notes Uganda met the criteria to end transmission after the 42-day period without new cases. Published August 27, 2026.

triage.headline_ja: ウガンダ、42日間新規エボラ感染なしと発表 コンゴでは感染者数が増加
triage.triage_reason: DRCで5,713例・2,744死亡と大規模なエボラ流行が6州に拡大中であり、既にウガンダへの越境感染歴もあることから国際的拡大リスクと深刻な公衆衛生影響が認められる。
triage.notes: ウガンダは42日間新規例なしでWHO基準によりアウトブレイク終息と判定されたが、感染源はDRCからの入国者であり、DRC国内の流行は依然拡大中（6州に拡大、Bundibugyoエボラウイルス）。ウガンダは対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations には含めていない。

article.articleHeadline: DSÖ Uganda'daki Ebola salgınının sona erdiğini doğruladı
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: WHO confirmed that the Ebola outbreak in Uganda has ended.
article.articleSummary: WHO Africa region Emergency Director Marie-Roseline Belizaire announced that Uganda's Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak has ended after 42 days with no new cases following the discharge of the last patient; monitoring continues to ensure no new transmission chains emerge. In the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), the Ebola outbreak persists and is now the nation's largest and deadliest. As of Monday, there are 5,656 confirmed cases and 2,715 deaths, with transmission still very active despite a slowing pace. Ituri province reports 246 suspected cases and 65 deaths; the outbreak was declared on May 15. The Bundibugyo variant has no approved treatment or vaccine. To sustain control efforts, $30 million is urgently needed for logistics, medical supplies, and PPE to the most affected regions; failure to fund could jeopardize interventions. Regional border areas remain at high risk.

triage.headline_ja: WHOはウガンダでのエボラ流行終息を確認したが、コンゴ民主共和国（DRC）ではエボラ流行が同国史上最大・最悪の規模で継続中
triage.triage_reason: DRCのエボラ流行は同国史上最大・最悪規模（5,656例、死亡2,715例）で、国境地域でのリスクや資金不足による対応停滞の懸念があり、IHR基準を複数満たすためフルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: ウガンダのブンディブギョ株流行は終息済みと報告されているが、記事URL（2018年10月13日付）や内容から、本記事は2018年当時の情報を再配信・誤配信した可能性が高い。ウガンダは対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations から除外。DRCの状況は現時点で継続的な監視・確認が必要。

article.articleHeadline: WHO nyatakan wabah ebola di Uganda berakhir usai nirkasus 42 hari
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: WHO declares Ebola outbreak in Uganda over after 42 days without new cases.
article.articleSummary: Uganda’s 2026 Ebola outbreak has been declared over after 42 consecutive days with no confirmed new cases. The World Health Organization (WHO) announced the end during a virtual briefing by the Africa Regional Office to mark day 42 since the last confirmed Ebola patient was discharged. Uganda first declared the outbreak on May 15 after confirming a single case imported from the Democratic Republic of Congo. In total, 20 laboratory-confirmed cases were reported, including 18 recoveries and 2 deaths. On July 28, Uganda’s Ministry of Health announced the outbreak had ended, stating epidemiological investigations and identified outbreak characteristics provided scientific evidence that transmission had ceased. The WHO assessment, as of August 26, 2026, confirms Uganda is free of Ebola. There is no reported further spread.

triage.headline_ja: WHO、ウガンダのエボラ流行終息を宣言—新規感染なしで42日経過
triage.triage_reason: ウガンダのエボラ流行はWHOにより終息が確認され、新規感染や拡大の報告はない。対象国（DRC）は輸入元としての言及のみで、実際の発生国はウガンダ（対象国リスト外）であるため、リスクは低い。
triage.notes: 記事はウガンダでのエボラ流行終息宣言に関する内容。DRCは初発例の輸入元として言及されているが、実際の発生・拡大はウガンダ国内に限定されており、DRCは対象国として含めない。ウガンダ自体はGeoNames対象国リストに含まれていないため、verified_locationsは空配列とした。

article.articleHeadline: 港大及懲教署合作為在囚人士篩查丙型肝炎　揭盛行率達4.1%高於一般人口 (17:37) - 20260827
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: HKU and the Correctional Services Department collaborate to screen inmates for Hepatitis C, revealing a prevalence of 4.1%, higher than that of the general population (17:37) - 2026-08-27
article.articleSummary: Hepatitis C virus (HCV) screening in Hong Kong prisons by HKU’s Medical School and the Correctional Services Department found a 4.1% prevalence among inmates, higher than the general population at 0.3%. HCV infection can progress to cirrhosis, hepatocellular carcinoma, and death. As of 2024, only 36% of infections are diagnosed, and among those diagnosed only 20% receive curative therapy; HCV-related deaths have risen over the past decade in Hong Kong. A 2023 pilot offered voluntary screening and treatment for eligible prisoners. Using pilot data, researchers simulated 10,000 inmates with decision trees and Markov models to assess the cost-effectiveness of prison screening and treatment versus screening in a control group. Findings show 100% success in coordinated care and viral eradication when linked to care, and both current inmates and new admissions benefit from one-off universal screening. Telemedicine is identified as an economical, scalable option to improve specialist access in prisons.

triage.headline_ja: 香港大学と懲教署が共同で在監者の丙型肝炎（C型肝炎）検査を実施　感染率4.1%と一般人口より高いことが判明 (17:37) - 2026年8月27日
triage.triage_reason: 研究・監視データに基づく学術的報告であり、急性の公衆衛生危機や国際的拡大リスクを示す要素がなく、慢性疾患の疫学調査結果に留まる。
triage.notes: 香港（中国特別行政区）の刑務所内でのC型肝炎（慢性血液媒介性感染症）のスクリーニング研究結果であり、急性感染症の集団発生ではない。ヒト-ヒト直接感染拡大のリスクは低く、既知の慢性疾患管理の文脈。

article.articleHeadline: Flu Singapura Mulai Merebak di Kepri, Dinkes Karimun Waspadai Mobilitas dari Malaysia dan Singapura
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Singapore Flu Begins to Spread in the Riau Islands, Karimun Health Office Warns of Mobility from Malaysia and Singapore.
article.articleSummary: Hand, Foot and Mouth Disease (HFMD), commonly called the Singapore Flu, is increasingly detected in the Riau Islands, Indonesia, as of August 27, 2026, with Batam reporting hundreds of cases. Karimun Regency Health Office says there are no confirmed HFMD cases yet in Karimun, but authorities are maintaining heightened vigilance because of proximity to Singapore and Malaysia. The shortest distance from Karimun Besar to Kukup, Malaysia is about 16 km, and to Singapore about 57–100 km. An elevated risk stems from mobility through international ports, prompting coordinated surveillance with the Port Health Office and other agencies at entry points. Symptoms start like ordinary flu, with fever and respiratory signs, then a rash on hands and feet and possibly mouth ulcers. Residents, especially children, are urged not to ignore symptoms and seek care promptly.

triage.headline_ja: リアウ諸島でシンガポールフルー（手足口病）が拡大、カリムン保健局がマレーシア・シンガポールからの人流に警戒
triage.triage_reason: 手足口病（HFMD）はインドネシア国内で例年見られる小児感染症であり、現時点で重症例の増加や国際的拡大の明確な兆候はないが、国境地域での人流を通じた継続的な感染リスクがあるため経過観察が必要。
triage.notes: 記事はインドネシア・リアウ諸島（バタム、カリムン）でのHFMD拡大に関するもの。シンガポール・マレーシアは近接国として言及されているが、対象国リストに含まれず、また記事の主題は両国での発生ではないため除外。HFMDは通常軽症で季節性のある疾患であり、重症度や異常性の観点からは特筆すべき要素は少ない。

The report highlights ongoing surveillance needs as Uganda ends its outbreak while the DRC experiences a growing one.

article.articleHeadline: H1N1, कोविड या टाइफाइड? एक जैसे हैं तीनों के शुरुआती लक्षण, जानिए कब करवाना चाहिए कौन-सा टेस्ट - h1n1 covid or typhoid all three share similar early symptoms know which test to get and when
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: H1N1, COVID-19 or Typhoid? All three have similar early symptoms; know which test to take and when.
article.articleSummary: In New Delhi, India, concurrent outbreaks of H1N1, COVID-19, and Typhoid produce overlapping early symptoms—high fever, headaches, fatigue, and body aches—yet no single sign distinguishes them. Cough and sore throat may appear with H1N1 or COVID-19, whereas Typhoid often starts with fever and mild nonspecific symptoms. Diagnosis relies on doctor-led evaluation and targeted testing: RT-PCR for H1N1/COVID-19 from respiratory samples early in illness; blood culture for Typhoid; the Widal test is not a definitive proof and should not alone guide antibiotics. Expensive respiratory multiplex panels are not required for every fever. Avoid self-minitiated antibiotics (azithromycin, amoxicillin) for viral illnesses. If H1N1 is suspected, start antivirals (oseltamivir) within 48 hours of symptoms; still beneficial for high-risk or severe cases beyond 48 hours. Seek urgent care for breathing difficulties, chest pain, confusion, or rapidly worsening symptoms, especially in elderly, children, diabetics, or asthma patients in India.

article.articleHeadline: Uganda ends Ebola outbreak following completion of 42-day countdown
article.articleSummary: Twenty confirmed Ebola virus disease cases caused by Bundibugyo virus were reported in Uganda from 15 May 2026, with 18 recoveries and 2 deaths. Fifteen cases were imported from the Democratic Republic of the Congo; five were locally acquired among contacts and health workers linked to imported cases. Uganda discharged the last imported patient on 16 July 2026 and announced interruption of local transmission on 28 July; a 42-day countdown without new locally acquired cases concluded the outbreak, meeting the international benchmark for declaring transmission ended. More than 800 contacts were identified and monitored. Actions included enhanced surveillance at health facilities and entry points, rapid case detection and confirmation, contact tracing, isolation, infection prevention and control, and community engagement, supported by joint Africa CDC/WHO efforts. The outbreak persists in DRC, with ongoing cross-border risk and emphasis on preparedness; WHO advises against travel/trade restrictions.

article.articleHeadline: Malaria outbreak kills two workers at Germany's busiest airport -- RT World News
article.articleSummary: Two Frankfurt Airport workers have died in a rare malaria outbreak linked to Anopheles mosquitoes apparently imported by plane from a malaria-endemic country. The outbreak began in early July 2026; the first death occurred shortly afterward, with diagnosis confirmed posthumously. The Robert Koch Institute (RKI) confirmed four cases among airport employees in mid-July; local media later reported a total of six male workers infected, mostly handling luggage. Frankfurt health authorities say the population risk remains very low and malaria is not transmitted person-to-person, only by mosquitoes. Authorities captured several mosquitoes at the airport and sent them for genetic analysis to determine origin; the outbreak is an example of "airport malaria," a phenomenon last seen at Frankfurt in 2023. Malaria symptoms include fever, chills, headaches, and fatigue; severe cases can cause organ failure. Global malaria deaths were about 610,000 in 2024, with most deaths in Nigeria, DRC, Niger.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: World Health Organization announces the end of the Ebola outbreak in Uganda.
article.articleSummary: World Health Organization has formally declared that the Ebola virus disease outbreak in Uganda has ended as of August 27, 2026. The confirmation contrasts with ongoing transmission in the neighboring Democratic Republic of Congo, where the outbreak remains active and regional vigilance remains high. The UN health agency notes continued containment efforts across the region, bolstering surveillance systems and rapid response to prevent new flare-ups. Uganda's handling of the outbreak is viewed as a potential regional model, highlighting lessons in outbreak detection, investigation, community engagement, and cross-border cooperation. The Congolese outbreak underscores persistent cross-border risks and the need for intensified regional and international collaboration to curb transmission, monitor potential introductions, and prevent future epidemics.

Results dated August 26, 2026 and received August 27, 2026 detected Salmonella, Streptococcus faecalis, and Bacillus cereus in nasi liwet; and Streptococcus faecalis and Bacillus cereus in telor balado. Ali Syofi'i, head of DKK Rembang, said results were only received today, and SMPN 5 Rembang principal Menik Mustikatun had not yet received the lab results or commented as of August 27, 2026. article.articleHeadline: Nepal Floods: Floodwater May Spread Infectious Diseases, How To Stay Safe
article.articleSummary: On August 26, a flash flood at the Nepal–Tibet border, triggered by a Himalayan glacier collapse, devastated parts of Nepal with many dead or missing as rescue teams search. Floodwater contaminates water and sanitation systems, raising infection risk. Infections to watch include diarrhoea, typhoid, hepatitis A, skin infections, leptospirosis, and tetanus from flood-related injuries. Precautions: avoid floodwater; if unavoidable, wear protective clothing; drink only safe water (bottled, boiled or treated) and discard flood-contaminated food; wash cuts with clean water and soap, cover wounds, and seek tetanus vaccination for deep/dirty injuries. Maintain hand hygiene; monitor for symptoms such as diarrhoea, vomiting, fever, abdominal pain, skin infections or weakness; seek medical care if symptoms persist or are severe. The article provides no laboratory confirmation or imported/exported case details.

article.articleHeadline: Suspect you have dengue? Kolkata doctors spell out symptoms and warning signs to watch for
article.articleSummary: Dengue in Kolkata, India, with the death of a 10-year-old boy from South Dum Dum after testing positive for dengue. Doctors emphasize early recognition: watch for sudden high-grade fever with headache (behind the eyes), shivering, abdominal discomfort, vomiting, or stomach upset. NS1 antigen testing is commonly used in the first five days; after day five, dengue IgM helps confirm infection. Molecular tests such as RT-PCR can detect infection early, with rapid platforms like Truenat available where accessible. Post-diagnosis, regular CBCs focusing on platelet count and haematocrit guide management; a falling platelet count with rising haematocrit indicates plasma leakage and risk of severe dengue. Physicians advise against self-medication or attempting to manage thrombocytopenia without medical supervision.

article.articleHeadline: RDC : l'OMS appelle à une trêve humanitaire face à Ebola
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: DRC: WHO calls for a humanitarian pause amid Ebola.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) caused by Bundibugyo ebolavirus prompts the World Health Organization (WHO) to seek a humanitarian pause of at least six months to guarantee safe, unimpeded access to affected communities and halt transmission. Access constraints are now the main impediment to the response, according to WHO Africa Region Director Dr. Mohamed Yakub Janabi. As of 21 August 2026, the DRC reports 5,514 confirmed Ebola cases and 2,642 deaths across 57 health zones, marking the second-largest and fastest-growing outbreak on record. Health-worker protection is a priority: 158 infected, 45 dead as of 20 August. Calls to double or triple response capacity emphasize enhanced case detection, contact tracing, infection prevention and control in health facilities, trained staff, PPE, and reliable water, plus expedited international deployment and investigations of deaths outside treatment centers. Additional measures include surveillance of movements, postponing large gatherings, border controls, safe school reopening, reduced crowding, and monitoring boats to Kinshasa; the outbreak remains a public health emergency of international concern with elevated regional risk.

article.articleHeadline: Hà Nội tăng cường giám sát, phòng chống sốt xuất huyết tại 32 phường, xã
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Hanoi strengthens surveillance and dengue fever prevention in 32 wards and communes.
article.articleSummary: 309 dengue fever cases were reported in Hanoi during 14–21 August 2026, across 65 wards/communes, down 7 from the previous week. Hanoi is strengthening dengue surveillance and prevention in 32 wards/communes. Cumulatively, Hanoi has recorded 1,907 dengue cases in 115 wards/communes in 2026, with no deaths. Despite this decline, 15 new outbreak clusters were detected this week, bringing total clusters to 78 since the start of the year, with 29 active. The Hanoi CDC and mobile outbreak teams conduct wide-area surveillance, including epidemiological investigations, vector monitoring, dengue serology and virus surveillance, and community case finding in districts such as Van Mieu-Quoc Tu Giam, Yen Hoa, Ha Dong, Chuong My, Dong Da, Hoan Kiem, Me Linh, Thanh Xuan, and Dai Mo. Preventive measures emphasize mosquito source reduction, bite protection, and prompt medical care for sudden fever, headache, myalgia, or rash; avoid self-medication.

Year-to-date, there are 65 notifications, 5 confirmed, 60 discarded, and no cases under investigation. The first confirmed case of 2026 was announced on March 10 through the CNIEV (National Center for Epidemiological Intelligence and Genomic Surveillance) dashboard, with records showing the first three infections contracted in February and the fourth in March. Despite ongoing new cases, the majority of notifications have been discarded, and authorities maintain permanent monitoring of the situation.

Officials emphasize vaccination as a key preventive measure against rabies, a potentially fatal viral disease transmitted via dog bites or scratches. KDMC Mayor Harshali Chaudhary urged citizens and animal lovers to cooperate, aiding teams in locating and vaccinating dogs. The drive is designed for sustained, long-term coverage rather than a one-off intervention, with the phased rollout progressively expanding across all municipal wards to reduce human rabies exposure.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Germs Found in the SPPG Pakisrejo Menu, Inspection Results Reveal Many Kitchen Problems.
article.articleSummary: Germs detected in the MBG menu linked to a mass food poisoning event in Pakisrejo Village, Rejotangan District, Tulungagung Regency, Indonesia, after meals on July 29, 2026. Laboratory tests confirmed the presence of micro-organisms causing mass illness, though the specific pathogen was not disclosed; the finding was discussed at a Tulungagung MBG Task Force coordination meeting and reported to the National Nutrition Agency (BGN) via the regional Korwil. An environmental health inspection at SPPG Pakisrejo uncovered sanitation gaps: toilets lacking hand-washing soap, open-plastic waste on-site, non-food-grade cleaning agents, a cramped utensil-washing area, and no dedicated space for incoming raw materials. Operators were urged to address all issues and secure the Sertifikat Laik Higiene Sanitasi (SLHS) to ensure hygiene and sanitation compliance.

article.articleHeadline: H1N1 से ठीक होकर फिर आ गया बुखार और खांसी? इसे मामूली समझने की भूल मत करना
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Recovered from H1N1, but fever and cough returned? Don’t mistake it for something minor.
article.articleSummary: In India, H1N1 (swine flu) symptoms can linger after the fever subsides; fatigue and mild cough may persist for days. Some patients experience a relapse, with fever returning or a more productive cough within a few days. Shortness of breath on exertion and chest heaviness can be part of recovery, and a slow return of strength is not unusual. Warning signs that require medical evaluation include fever returning with worse cough, breathing difficulty, chest pain, or a change in sputum color, which may signal pneumonia or another infection. Do not self-medicate with antibiotics for a suspected relapse; H1N1 is viral and antibiotics are not always needed. Vulnerable groups—elderly, infants, pregnant women, and people with heart, asthma, or chronic lung disease—should vaccinate and seek care promptly. Rest, fluids, and proper nutrition are essential; consult a doctor if symptoms worsen or fail to improve.

article.articleSummary: World Health Organization declares end of the Ebola outbreak in Uganda caused by the Bundibugyo strain after 20 infections and 2 deaths; Uganda had announced on July 28 it was disease-free.
